direct injection of plasmid DNA can result in a high transfection efficiency in mouse and human melanoma and cervical carcinoma.
direct injection of naked DNA into mouse melanomas can result in a high and persistent level of transfection.
direct injection of free DNA can be used for transfecting tumor cells and that this method can be used to study the mechanism of gene expression in vivo.

the use of free DNA as an effective gene transfer agent for cancer gene therapy and the optimization of the conditions for gene transfer.
the use of direct injection of naked DNA as an efficient and simple approach for cancer gene therapy.

the transfection efficiency by direct gene transfer is highly variable, depending on tumor type, promoter used, and other factors.
direct injection of free DNA is a simple, effective and promising approach for cancer gene therapy.
the direct injection into tumors of plasmid DNA encoding a reporter gene is an effective method to achieve long term expression.

the direct injection is a very simple and effective method for cancer gene delivery, but it is still far from being an effective method for gene therapy.

the direct injection method can be applied to a variety of tumor types, but the efficiency of transfection is tumor type dependent.
